usamo-usamo-1983-01.prompt: On a given circle, six points $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$, and $F$ are chosen at random, independently and uniformly with respect to arc length. Determine the probability that the two triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ are disjoint, i.e., have no common points.

usamo-usamo-1983-02.prompt:
Prove that the roots of
$$x^5 + ax^4 + bx^3 + cx^2 + dx + e = 0$$
cannot all be real if $2a^2 < 5b$.
usamo-usamo-1983-02.answer: If all roots $x_i$ are real, Vieta gives $2a^2-5b = \tfrac12\sum_{i<j}(x_i-x_j)^2 \ge 0$, i.e. $2a^2\ge 5b$.

usamo-usamo-1983-03.prompt: Each set of a finite family of subsets of a line is a union of two closed intervals. Moreover, any three of the sets of the family have a point in common. Prove that there is a point which is common to at least half the sets of the family.
usamo-usamo-1983-03.answer: Write $S_i = [a_i,b_i]\cup[c_i,d_i]$ with $b_i\le c_i$; then every set contains $\alpha=\max a_i$ or $\delta=\min d_i$ (a set missing both could not share a point with the sets attaining $\alpha$ and $\delta$), so one of these two points lies in at least half the sets.

usamo-usamo-1983-04.prompt: Six segments $S_1, S_2, S_3, S_4, S_5,$ and $S_6$ are given in a plane. These are congruent to the edges $AB, AC, AD, BC, BD,$ and $CD$, respectively, of a tetrahedron $ABCD$. Show how to construct a segment congruent to the altitude of the tetrahedron from vertex $A$ with straight-edge and compasses.
usamo-usamo-1983-04.answer: Draw face $BCD$; fold faces $ABC$ and $ABD$ into its plane (getting $A_1, A_2$); the perpendiculars from $A_1$ to $BC$ and from $A_2$ to $BD$ meet at the foot $H$ of the altitude; with $F$ the foot on $BC$, the altitude is the leg $\sqrt{A_1F^2-FH^2}$ of a right triangle.

usamo-usamo-1983-05.prompt: Consider an open interval of length $1/n$ on the real number line, where $n$ is a positive integer. Prove that the number of irreducible fractions $p/q$, with $1\le q\le n$, contained in the given interval is at most $(n+1)/2$.
usamo-usamo-1983-05.answer: Two such fractions in the interval cannot have denominators $q$ and $kq$ (their difference would be $\ge \frac1{kq}\ge\frac1n$), so the denominators are distinct and no one divides another; grouping $1,\dots,n$ by odd part shows there are at most $\lceil n/2\rceil$ of them.
